title: Built an early-warning and market intelligence terminal for US Equities & Crypto to eliminate fragmented research
author: -Omrr_Utku12
selftext:
Hey everyone,

Like most active traders, my biggest bottleneck was always analysis paralysis caused by fragmented data. Trying to manually reconcile balance sheet solvency, institutional filings, on-chain tokenomics, and breaking headlines across five different tabs usually means either executing emotionally or getting into trades way too late.

I built **Aixio** to solve this exact problem—an objective analysis, classification, and early-warning terminal that brings equities and crypto into a structured, unified workflow. It’s an actively evolving tool that I’m tuning daily to help myself and fellow traders cut down research hours without sacrificing depth.

Here is how the analytical engine evaluates and scores both markets under the hood:

**US Equities Forensic & Fundamental Evaluation:** Instead of relying on surface-level metrics, the system calculates an institutional-grade breakdown across balance sheet health, valuation, and capital flow:

**Accounting & Solvency Models:** Computes Beneish M-Score to detect manipulation red flags, Altman Z-Score for bankruptcy risk, and Piotroski F-Score to measure operational momentum. 

**Capital Quality & Fair Value:** Evaluates Return on Invested Capital (ROIC), DuPont ROE decomposition, Economic Value Added (EVA), Free Cash Flow (FCF) yield, and Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) intrinsic fair value. 

**Valuation & Debt Structure:** Combines Debt/Equity ratios, traditional multiples (P/E, P/B), and PEG ratios (GARP) to price growth accurately. 

**Smart Money Tracking:** Directly cross-references these forensic scores with SEC Form 4 insider transactions, 13F whale fund institutional positioning, and consensus Wall Street analyst price targets.

**Verifiable Crypto Realities (On-Chain Fundamentals):** Filters out social media hype to focus strictly on real on-chain health and cash flows:

**Fee Revenue & P/E Equivalent:** Tracks 24-hour protocol fee revenue (identifying real "Cash Cow" protocols like LDO and TRX) and compares them against market cap. JPG

**Capital Backing (TVL & MCAP/TVL):** Evaluates total deposited funds (TVL) and the MCAP/TVL ratio to assess whether an asset is fundamentally overvalued or undervalued relative to actual usage. JPG

**Circulating Supply vs. Future Unlock Risks:** Tracks upcoming cliff unlocks and computes the immediate volume shock percentage (e.g., flagging upcoming 50%+ supply shocks) before selling pressure hits spot price. 

**News Sentiment Score:** Real-time NLP scores breaking headlines into clear impact points (+15 / -15) to see if narrative momentum aligns with on-chain realities. JPG

**Automated Market Regimes & Structural Buckets:** Classification algorithms automatically group assets based on their quantitative signatures:

*Equities:* Fast-Growing Bargain Stocks (GARP), Macro Shield Defense (low-debt, cash-rich balance sheets), and institutional accumulation setups. 

*Crypto:* Squeezed Sellers (high-probability short-squeeze setups) and Low Developer Unlock Pressure (assets with over 90% circulating supply). 

**Early Warning Push Notifications:** Whenever an asset's technical or fundamental score deteriorates, a negative news narrative confirms a breakdown, or an upcoming token supply shock approaches, the system triggers an immediate push alert before the broader market reacts. JPG+ 1

**Multi-Horizon Model Portfolios:** Generates automated model portfolios tailored to your risk profile (Safe Haven, Balanced Growth, Aggressive) across short, mid, and long-term horizons by balancing asset health against active volume momentum. 

**1-Tap LLM Synthesis:** When you don’t have time to dig through dozens of financial ratios, an embedded LLM synthesizes the underlying health scores, momentum, and live news into a structured 3-bullet briefing: Conviction & Bias, key risk factors, and a Strategic Verdict. JPG

The app is live on both stores with a 7-day trial:

**iOS:** [https://apps.apple.com/us/app/aixio-ai-stocks-crypto/id6802835226](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/aixio-ai-stocks-crypto/id6802835226)

**Android:** [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.finanscepte.app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.finanscepte.app&hl=en-US&ah=q4vT4KURVYYmHsEt8LXvb5P-E_A) 

I’m constantly refining the models and data feeds based on real trading scenarios. Would love to get your thoughts on the workflow, UI, and any specific metrics or alternative data feeds you rely on daily!

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body: The cross-asset normalization seems worth testing before the Safe Haven, Balanced Growth, and Aggressive portfolios are judged. Beneish M-Score and Altman Z-Score have very different base rates from MCAP/TVL or a +15/-15 headline score, so how are they calibrated into comparable conviction? I’d publish an ablation showing portfolio turnover and drawdown with each score family removed, plus alert precision by trigger type. No image was available here; I’d want to inspect the displayed component weights and timestamps before evaluating the UI.

replies.author: -Omrr_Utku12
replies.body: Appreciate the sharp critique—this is exactly the level of technical pushback I was hoping for. To clear up the architectural premise, the two markets don't share a single normalized scoring pool at all. The US equities and crypto engines run as completely decoupled, isolated pipelines with their own domain-specific baselines, so I'm never calibrating something like a Beneish score against MCAP/TVL or trying to force them onto the same scale. Within each pipeline, the weights are strictly hierarchical: deep forensic health and balance sheet metrics carry vastly more weight than news NLP, meaning a transient +15/-15 headline score can never override fundamentally broken solvency. The portfolio frameworks were dialed in through iterative feature inclusion and exclusion to keep turnover and drawdown reasonable rather than just slapping disparate metrics together. As for the unlock alerts, they aren't static triggers; the engine models an estimated liquidity absorption ratio by evaluating the upcoming cliff unlock directly against the asset’s 24-hour real volume and market depth, and that absorption capacity is broken down on the asset detail view so you can see if the market can realistically digest the dilution. That's completely on me, by the way—totally slipped my mind and I forgot to attach the screenshots when posting, but I’d be glad to share them so you can inspect the actual component weights and timestamps in the UI.

comments.author: koryuken
comments.body: Why should i pay for this when anyone with Claude code can do the same brief as a scheduled task?

replies.author: -Omrr_Utku12
replies.body:
Fair point, a scheduled task is enough for a one-off summary. But I'm not producing summaries. I couldn't track hundreds of crypto and US stock tickers by hand, so I handed that to software. A worker runs in the background and keeps scoring every asset.

On crypto, the score starts with BTC's health and each coin's strength against it. From there it weighs breakouts (fresh ones, not highs that keep failing), volume that builds over days, hidden accumulation, bull flags, futures positioning like funding rate and open interest, order book depth, token burns and dozens more. It also penalizes coins that already ran too far, and drops trap candles and stablecoins up front.

On US stocks, it combines trend and volume signals with risk metrics (Sharpe, Sortino, max drawdown) and balance sheet checks like Altman Z, Beneish M, Piotroski, ROIC, buybacks and insider buying, plus VIX and DXY for the market regime.

These offset each other. A stock can spike on volume and still lose points if its accounting looks shaky. Assets are grouped by these scores and everything updates as new data arrives.

News works the same way. I don't judge it by tone. After a headline I check whether price and volume actually reacted (with BTC's move subtracted) and ignore it if the market didn't care.

And it isn't a finished product. I'm actively working on it every day, tuning the scoring and fixing what the logs show, so it gets more accurate and reliable with each iteration. Both the tool and the way it's being developed are moving fast.

comments.author: wisesheets
comments.body: Beneish and Piotroski need clean statements, so data quality must matter a lot here. Which provider feeds the fundamentals, and how often do you catch bad numbers?
